summary: Ralph Lilley Turner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1907-1913). He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (1920-1922) and the University of London (~1922-1957), where he also served as Director of SOAS (1922-1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (BA ~1843-1846) under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1849) and Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861-1876).
Ralph Waldo Emerson was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Harvard College (~1817-1821), Harvard Divinity School (~1825-1826), and Harvard University (~1817-1826).
Ram Chandra Dhungana was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Assistant Editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).

Ram Chandra Kak worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Sri Pratap College and under John Marshall. He was an Archaeological Survey of India superintendent (~1914-1919) and served as Jammu and Kashmir's Chief Secretary and archaeological superintendent (1919-1929).

Ram Chandra Pandeya was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti. At the University of Delhi, he was Head of Buddhist Studies (~1966-1973) and an acharya (~1973-1996).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his MA at Patna University and his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974-1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984-1985).

Ram Mohan Roy worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), Brahmo Samaj (1828), and the Calcutta Unitarian Committee.

Ram Niwas Pandey, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Bhattacharya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Swami Dharmamegha Aranya and Raghunatha Shastri. He served as a research assistant at Banaras Hindu University and the All-India Kashiraj Trust, and as a teacher at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya.

Ram Shankar Tripathi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He headed the Buddhist philosophy department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1974-1998) and served as Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1998-2004).

Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He headed the history departments at Patna University (1958-1973) and the University of Delhi (~1973-1985) and founded the Indian Council of Historical Research.

Rama Mishra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, serving as Professor (attested 1882-1889) and as assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya (attested 1914).

Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, completing his PhD at the University of Rochester (~1971). He held professorships at the University of Rochester (1971-1976) and the University of Hawaiʻi (1976).

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug, earning a PhD from Göttingen (1885). He held professorships at Elphinstone College and Deccan College, and was Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893-1894).

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist who worked in the Sadholal research division at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as Head of the Veda Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Scottish Church College (BA ~1896). He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1917-1919) and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (1921-1932).
Ramaprasada Tripathi was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held affiliations at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested in 1976 and 2001).

Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who completed his degrees at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Sanskrit department head at Jadavpur, vice chancellor at the University of Burdwan (1970-1984) and Rabindra Bharati University, and chancellor of National Sanskrit University.

Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith, L. D. Arts College (attested 1938), and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (attested 1938).
